purpose: Cefprozil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including ear infections, throat infections like strep throat, sinus infections, and some skin infections. It works specifically against bacteria, so it will not help with viral infections like the common cold or flu. Your doctor prescribed it to help your body fight off a specific bacterial infection you have.
how_it_works: Cefprozil works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of it like removing the protective shell around the bacteria — without that wall, the bacteria cannot survive and eventually die off. This helps clear the infection from your body over the course of your treatment.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, upset stomach, and vomiting. Some people may notice a mild skin rash or itching. You might also experience dizziness or headache. These effects are usually mild and tend to go away on their own as your body adjusts.
warnings: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to penicillin antibiotics, as there is a small chance you could also be allergic to cefprozil. Stop taking it and seek medical help right away if you develop a severe rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, since your dose may need to be adjusted. Also, taking antibiotics can sometimes cause a serious intestinal condition called C. difficile — contact your doctor if you develop severe or persistent diarrhea.
typical_dosing: For adults and teenagers, the usual dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth once or twice a day, depending on the type of infection. For children, the dose is based on their weight and is typically given once or twice daily. It can be taken with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal. Always finish your full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
